note: Licences a corpus source may carry. Anything not listed here is excluded, including every licence whose id is absent rather than merely unlisted. V2 §5 P1 fixes the shape of this list: public domain and CC0, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, MIT/Apache/BSD-licensed documentation, and government works whose terms permit reuse. NonCommercial and NoDerivatives are excluded outright — not downgraded, not flagged, excluded — because a corpus that cannot be reused commercially cannot back a commercial product, and a corpus that cannot be derived from cannot be turned into procedures.

excluded_by_policy.reason: The product is commercial. A corpus carrying NC terms cannot back it, and the restriction survives every downstream copy.
A procedure corpus is a derivative work by construction: documents are split into passages, summarised, and paired with suggested replies. ND forbids exactly that.
An unstated licence is not a permissive one. Absence of terms is treated as all rights reserved, which is the default in copyright.

public-domain.name: Public domain
public-domain.note: Includes works of the US federal government under 17 U.S.C. §105.

CC-BY-SA-4.0.name: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International
CC-BY-SA-4.0.note: ShareAlike propagates to derived corpora. A corpus built from a CC-BY-SA source must itself carry CC-BY-SA, which is recorded in its attribution file.

OGL-3.0.name: Open Government Licence v3.0
OGL-3.0.note: Crown copyright. Attribution statement required; the attribution file carries the exact wording the licence prescribes.
